title.en: Nutrition in plants and human beings
Where does the energy come from?

text.en: A plant sits in the sun and makes its own food, while we must eat. Both kinds of living things need nutrition to stay alive.

Life processes are the basic functions that keep an organism alive: nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion.
Autotrophs make their own food by photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O in sunlight and chlorophyll gives glucose + 6O2.
Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll, sunlight, carbon dioxide and water. Stomata let in CO2 and release oxygen.
Heterotrophs depend on others for food. Examples are holozoic nutrition in humans, saprophytic nutrition in fungi and parasitic nutrition in cuscuta.
In humans, digestion starts in the mouth where salivary amylase breaks starch into sugar. The food travels through the oesophagus to the stomach.
The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid, which kills bacteria and activates pepsin, and mucus protects the stomach wall.
In the small intestine bile from the liver emulsifies fats and pancreatic juice has trypsin, lipase and amylase. Villi absorb digested food.
The large intestine absorbs water, and undigested food leaves the body through the anus.

problem.en: Why is bile secreted although it contains no enzymes?

text.en: Bile contains salts that make the medium alkaline for enzymes of the pancreas.
It also breaks large fat globules into smaller ones, which is emulsification.

prompt.en: What is the path and chemistry of nutrition?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking digestion ends in the stomach

points.en: Autotrophs photosynthesise; heterotrophs depend on others.
Digestive enzymes: amylase, pepsin, trypsin, lipase.
Villi in the small intestine increase surface area for absorption.
